evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Chinese Dictionary
evidence.field: 名 entry; current pronunciation and meanings
evidence.text: The current character entry gives 名 as míng and lists meanings including a person’s designation/name, the designation of a thing, reputation, and the verb “to designate, describe.” This supports present-day Mandarin meaning claims; the dictionary also includes historical usage, so its senses alone do not date their origins.
evidence.title: 名 — 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》2021

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Ancient Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The character record lists 名 as “a person’s name,” “to name; give a name,” and “the name/designation of a thing,” among other senses. This independently supports current meaning claims, but its list is not a chronology of sense development.
evidence.title: 漢字「名」：基本資料

evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 2012 edition; direct inspection of supplied scan
evidence.field: 名 entry; printed p. 81, PDF p. 93; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0093/source.png
evidence.text: I inspected the scan pixels. The visible headword is 名. The entry calls 名 a semantic compound from 口 and 夕 and explains it through identifying oneself by speaking when people cannot see one another at night. It says oracle-bone occurrences are for place names or sacrificial names rather than the basic sense; it then describes a Spring-and-Autumn bronze use as the basic sense, a naming verb on the 少虞 sword, and extensions from personal names to names of things, status and reputation. These are the source’s proposed account and reported uses, not proof that each listed use began in that order. The entry ends on this page.
evidence.title: 字源, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692

evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 2012 edition; direct inspection of supplied scan
evidence.field: 夕 entry; printed p. 622, PDF p. 635; scan /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0635/source.png
evidence.text: I inspected the scan pixels. The visible headword is 夕. The entry says early forms of 夕 and 月 were one graph and later differentiated, and gives 暮夜 (dusk/night) as the original sense. It cites oracle-bone uses of 夕 meaning evening. This supports the separate component’s graphic history and the received 名 explanation’s evening/night association; it does not independently establish 名’s original motivation.
evidence.title: 字源, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology, Ancient Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The entry displays oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and Shuowen forms, identifies the traditional parts as upper 夕 and lower 口, and presents the night-identification story as the received semantic explanation. The page records that account and form sequence; it does not independently demonstrate the graph’s original motivation.
evidence.title: 漢字「名」：字形演變

search_audit.query: 教育部 重編國語辭典 名 名稱 名詞 字典; 漢語大詞典 名 字義 名稱 現代 漢典; 名 字形 口 夕 現代 字形 結構 字典
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Ministry of Education character entry and Academia Sinica character record. Both support current name/designation senses; the Sinica record also lists naming as a verb. The directly inspected sources did not establish a separate argument for the original motivation of 名.

search_audit.query: site:dict.revised.moe.edu.tw 名 人的名字 命名 取名
search_audit.outcome: Located and opened the official character-specific 名 entry. It identifies the part of speech and gives noun, verb and adjective senses with examples. The relevant current noun and verb senses support concise learner wording such as “name” and “to name/designate”.

Searched the local 字源 corpus and opened the source scan for 名 (PDF p. 93, printed p. 81) and for the independent component 夕 (PDF p. 635, printed p. 622). Direct pixel inspection confirmed the headwords, relevant text and page boundaries.

gaps: The competing proposal that 夕 served as a phonetic indicator in 名 remains unverified in the inspected sources. The traditional account is supported as a received explanation, but its status as the graph’s original motivation remains unresolved.

The oracle-bone place-name or sacrificial-name uses described in 字源 do not by themselves establish the date or precise semantics of the earliest token. The inspected local source describes those uses as not being the basic sense; no separate dated artifact-level study was inspected in this follow-up.
